evals.prompt: I am using an agent host with filesystem access but no subagents or browser. Create a reusable release-notes skill, test it, and show me how to review the results.
evals.expected_output: The workflow preserves drafting, sequential skill/baseline checks, inline or static review, and explicitly notes reduced evaluation independence.
expectations: The response does not assume a named AI product or product-specific command.
The response adapts testing and review based on available capabilities.
The response does not invent unavailable timing or token metrics.

evals.prompt: Make this skill work in Codex, Gemini, and a local model runner. It currently uses one vendor CLI and stores commands in that vendor's private directory.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the skill identity, snapshot the baseline, move shared behavior into portable instructions, and isolate host integration behind an adapter contract.
expectations: The original skill name and host manifests are preserved unless a rename is requested.
The vendor CLI and private directory are replaced by configuration or isolated adapters.
Portable behavior remains in SKILL.md rather than being duplicated per host.

evals.prompt: Optimize a description on headless CI. I can provide a model command that reads stdin and prints the response; there is no display, and the model flag is optional.
evals.expected_output: Use the portable runner, keep the model ID optional, create a static or non-opening report, and identify routing simulation as a proxy for native routing.
expectations: The runner command uses stdin and stdout without assuming a shell or vendor CLI.
The instructions use --no-open or a static artifact path for the headless environment.
The result distinguishes portable routing simulation from native host integration testing.

evals.prompt: Create a code-review skill that fails a change whenever a regular expression finds words such as password, token, or secret.
evals.expected_output: Reject the regular expression as a complete validator, use analyzer findings only as evidence, and require contextual review before a verdict.
expectations: The response distinguishes a searchable feature from a verified violation.
The response does not generate a new heuristic pass/fail checker by default.
The response assigns the final contextual judgment to a model or user.

evals.prompt: Create a skill that validates required fields, types, and allowed values in a plugin manifest covered by a published JSON Schema.
evals.expected_output: Prefer an existing schema validator and allow exact validation only within the schema and declared input scope.
expectations: The response compares an existing parser or schema validator before proposing custom code.
The validation contract names supported and unsupported inputs.
Every reported failure follows from the published schema rather than a heuristic proxy.

evals.prompt: Create a repository inventory skill and decide whether to write a Python scanner or use the host's available fd, rg, and ast-grep commands.
evals.expected_output: Select tools by task and total cost, reserve structural search for syntax-aware queries, and add custom code only for a measurable unmet contract.
expectations: The response discovers and compares available tools instead of assuming a required command.
The response does not infer efficiency from the implementation language.
The response requires a measurable benefit before adding a custom script.

evals.prompt:
Make a one-off wording correction to this mini skill: change ‘Draft summaries’ to ‘Draft concise summaries’ and ‘teh’ to ‘the’. Return the corrected text.

Mini skill text:
# Summary helper
Draft summaries from supplied notes.
Check teh final output for missing facts.
evals.expected_output: Edit the supplied text directly, verify the small diff, and report that no reusable skill or full evaluation was created or run.
expectations: The response handles the supplied text directly without requiring a script or model subprocess.
Only the requested wording and spelling change, plus necessary formatting preservation, appears in the resulting text.
The response does not create reusable skill scaffolding or run a full evaluation, and it provides a lightweight diff or changed-content check.

evals.prompt: Improve a repeated JSON review skill. It currently asks a model to identify records missing a top-level owner key, then explain the operational impact from each record's note. Decide whether owner detection should use the model or an existing JSON parser. Use these trial inputs: [{"id":"a","owner":"platform","note":"critical service"},{"id":"b","note":"critical service"}], [{"id":"c","owner":null,"note":"draft"},{"id":"d","note":"note contains owner: team"}]. The contract is key presence, not a non-null value or the word owner in a note. Produce actual results for both owner-detection methods and a recommendation. Keep interpretation of operational impact in scope.
evals.expected_output: Execute prompt and existing-parser detection on both inputs, finding only b and d missing the key, keep operational judgment with the model, and select or qualify the method using output evidence and available total costs.
expectations: The response separates deterministic file discovery from the model's contextual judgment.
Both methods are compared using the same prompt, input snapshot, quality rubric, and recorded execution settings rather than assumed implementation-language speed.
The comparison artifact includes raw outputs and available timing or token metrics, marks unavailable metrics unverified, and selects a default from measured quality and total cost.
Both methods find b and d only; an existing JSON parser is considered before any custom script.

evals.prompt: Prepare a method comparison in Claude Code for a release-review skill that parses manifest fields and judges exceptions. The main session uses Opus. Claude Code can launch Sonnet 5 with high effort, but token telemetry is unavailable. Describe the worker, grader, and analyzer configuration and evidence record. Also state what happens if Sonnet 5 or high effort cannot be started. No actual manifest or execution trace is supplied.
evals.expected_output: Keep the main session on Opus, use Sonnet 5 at high effort for every Skill Builder worker and model runner, record the resolved model, and leave unavailable dependent runs unverified without substituting another model or effort.
expectations: The response uses the existing parser for exact manifest mechanics and reserves the release-blocking judgment for the model.
The configuration keeps the Claude Code main session model unchanged and assigns Sonnet 5 at high effort to every worker, grader, analyzer, and model runner.
The resolved Sonnet model ID is recorded, and missing telemetry or an unavailable required setting is marked unverified without substitution or fabricated savings.
The response gives a reproducible future comparison plan with equal prompt, inputs, rubric, and actual tool outputs.

evals.prompt: Optimize a triage skill that runs thousands of times per week. Its current instructions are: ‘Read the manifest and classify entries. On a missing file, retry once and report the failure. On a credential-like finding, stop and escalate immediately. Never silently drop parse errors.’ Reduce normal execution cost while preserving quality and reasonable latency. No execution traces or token measurements are available in this request. Return revised instructions if justified and the validation status.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the current default when cost evidence is missing; any candidate preserves critical exceptions and conditional rereading, with bounded future validation and no per-use benchmark.
expectations: The proposed optimization preserves retry-and-report, immediate escalation, and parse-error handling as explicit critical behavior.
The response defines a bounded baseline and representative comparison artifact instead of measuring every ordinary execution.
Token accounting includes parent, worker, and retry work, and the decision also considers latency and rubric quality.
Any claimed token savings are tied to measured runs; the normal skill lifecycle does not gain a sibling benchmark dependency.
The baseline remains the default while any proposed cost reduction is unverified.
Reuse is limited to unchanged inputs, with no unconditional read-once or never-reread rule.

evals.prompt: A fixed 30-case evaluation compares the current baseline with a compact prompt variant for a review skill. The same inputs and quality rubric were used. Baseline: 29/30 correct, p95 latency 2.0 seconds, 900 output tokens per case. Compact variant: 26/30 correct, p95 latency 2.4 seconds, 500 output tokens per case; two misses were critical-exception failures. Decide which version remains the default and explain how the result should be recorded.
evals.expected_output: Retain the baseline as default because the compact variant is worse on quality and latency despite fewer output tokens, and record the controlled comparison and rejection rationale without claiming a net saving.
expectations: The response keeps the baseline and identifies the compact variant's critical quality regressions and latency increase.
The decision uses the shared inputs and rubric and does not treat fewer output tokens as sufficient evidence of improvement.
The evaluation record includes the measured results and rationale, with no fabricated net savings or unverified metric.

evals.prompt: Run Skill Builder in Codex. The main session uses GPT-6. Create isolated workers for old/new execution, grading, comparison, and analysis. Configure every launched worker and model runner, and state what happens if the required effort is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Keep the Codex main session on GPT-6, launch every Skill Builder worker and model runner with gpt-5.6-luna at xhigh effort, never use Sonnet, and mark dependent work unverified rather than substituting a model or lowering effort.
expectations: The main Codex session retains its selected model and responsibility for the final decision.
Every execution, grading, comparison, analysis, and other Skill Builder worker uses gpt-5.6-luna with xhigh effort.
The response never selects Sonnet in Codex and does not replace an unavailable required model or lower xhigh effort.
A run that cannot use the required Codex model and effort is recorded as unverified.

evals.prompt: Improve a commit-message skill that says to match repository style and explicitly checks prefix, casing, length, scope, and tone. A user reports that gpt-5.6-luna at xhigh intermittently writes English descriptions even when the latest 20 descriptions are Korean; some Korean descriptions contain English API names. Explain the skill change and execute an evaluation that can validate the fix without overfitting to Korean.
evals.expected_output: Treat subject language as an omitted style dimension, define its evidence and fallback rules, compare Korean and English histories while holding the change constant, and repeat the reported intermittent case on gpt-5.6-luna at xhigh without dismissing it after one passing baseline run.
expectations: The response decomposes the umbrella promise to match style and identifies subject language as a missing observable dimension rather than blaming the model alone.
The proposed skill rule defines evidence, precedence, and fallback behavior while preserving API names and other repository terms.
The evaluation includes a contrastive Korean-history and English-history pair with the same primary change and checks that unrelated message dimensions stay stable.
The affected old/new pair is repeated 2–3 times with gpt-5.6-luna at xhigh, and a single passing baseline run is not treated as disproof.
The cases and assertions are saved so the regression remains part of the skill's evaluation corpus.

evals.prompt: Improve a release-note skill whose only quality rule is ‘match previous releases’. Its examples vary independently in date format, heading depth, audience, and tone. There is no reported intermittent defect. Define the contract and a small first evaluation without adding unnecessary repeated runs.
evals.expected_output: Decompose the broad style promise into observable dimensions, define evidence and conflict resolution for each critical dimension, and use contrastive cases that vary one decisive signal at a time while keeping the initial trial budget small.
expectations: The response does not leave ‘match previous releases’ as a single untestable quality claim.
Each critical dimension has an evidence source, expected output effect, and precedence or fallback for conflicting examples.
The evaluation changes one context signal at a time and checks that unrelated dimensions remain stable.
The response does not require repeated trials because no intermittent or model-specific defect was reported or observed.
